newsitem.title: USA: US Q3 home prices up 1.7 pct--Freddie Mac.
newsitem.headline: US Q3 home prices up 1.7 pct--Freddie Mac.

text.p: Home prices nationwide rose at an annualized rate of 1.7 percent in the third quarter compared with the second quarter, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp said Monday.
The Conventional Mortgage Home-Price Index showed that annual house price appreciation increased by 3.7 percent from the third quarter of 1995, Freddie Mac said.
The quarterly index was jointly developed by Freddie Mac and the Federal National Mortgage Association, known as Fannie Mae.

House prices increased in five of the nine census divisions in the third quarter, led by the East North Central states, which showed a 6.5 percent gain at an annualized rate, Freddie Mac said. That region included Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, Ohio, and Wisconsin.
The West North Central states of Iowa, Kansas, Minnesota, Missouri, North Dakota, Nebraska and South Dakota showed a 4.9 percent increase annualized.
Home values in the East South Central region of Alabama, Kentucky, Mississippi and Tennessee rose 2.6 percent annualized.
Home values rose 2.4 percent annualized in the Mountain region, which included Arizona, Colorado, Idaho, Montana, New Mexico, Nevada, Utah and Wyoming.

In the South Atlantic home values rose at a 1.0 percent annualized rate, Freddie Mac said. That region included the District of Columbia, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Maryland, North Carolina, South Carolina, Virginia, and West Virginia.

The Pacific region, which included California, led regional declines with a 1.9 percent drop at an annualized rate, Freddie Mac said. Other states in that region were Alaska, Hawaii, Oregon and Washington.
New England and the West South Central region both showed a 1.8 percent drop in home prices at an annualized rate in the third quarter, Freddie Mac said.
New England included Connecticut, Massachusetts, Maine, New Hampshire, Rhode Island and Vermont. The West South Central states were Arkansas, Louisiana, Oklahoma, and Texas.
The Middle Atlantic region of New Jersey, New York and Pennsylvania posted a 0.8 percent drop on an annualized basis.
